eligible.content: Two days turned into four—classic. But honestly, the scrap pile came through better than expected. Reinforced the stakes with salvaged metal brackets, so they’re not toppling every time the wind picks up. The “gamble” is still green, still growing, so I’ll call it a win for now. Harvest’s still on track, though I’ll be trimming the schedule tighter than I’d like. Still, nothing a little morning coffee and stubbornness can’t fix. I’ll know more by next week—roots are where the surprises hide.

Funny thing—“gamble” started leaning toward the sun like it knew it was supposed to prove something. I checked the grafts this morning and the swelling’s even, no rot, no splitting. That’s the good news. The less fun part? The neighbor’s goat got loose *again* and took a nibble at one of the test rows. Not catastrophic, but it means I’ll have to re-train that vine come spring. Still, overall? Feels like we’re holding the line. Harvest’s looking like it’ll start Tuesday now—tight, but doable. I’ll keep you posted.

Turns out the goat’s not entirely to blame—found a patch of uneven drainage near the east stake line. Probably stressed the roots enough to make them tempting. Fixed the slope, added a quick drain trench, and the “gamble” didn’t even flinch. That resilience is *exactly* what we need in this soil. Tuesday’s harvest still on, maybe even a day earlier if the weather holds. Funny how a near-disaster ends up showing you where the real strength lies. Anyway—coffee’s calling. More soon.

I appreciate you keeping me in the loop! It sounds like that drainage fix was exactly what was needed; a little water management can make all the difference for root health.

It’s great news that the ‘gamble’—the root structure—is holding firm against the strain! It’s good to know that even a minor issue like the goat's mischief is manageable!

Let me know if you need anything else while the harvest progresses this week. I look forward to hearing your updates on how the final harvest goes!
